title: An American Tail
tagline: Off the boat and straight to the cheese.
about: A young mouse emigrates to New York and gets separated from his family.

    StartersFievel's potato latkesCrisp grated potato and onion pancakesHow to make it800g potatoes1 onion2 eggs3 tbsp plain flour250ml vegetable oil, for frying150g sour cream200g apple saucesalt, to tasteGrate the potatoes and onion and squeeze out the liquid well.Mix with the eggs, flour and salt.Fry spoonfuls in hot oil until crisp, turning once. Work in batches.Serve with sour cream and apple sauce.Beef and dill pirozhkiSoft yeast dough buns filled with seasoned beef, onion and dillHow to make it400g plain flour7g dried yeast250ml warm milk1 tsp caster sugar30g butter400g beef mince1 onion1 small bunch dill1 tbsp oilMix the flour, yeast, warm milk, sugar and butter into a soft dough and knead briefly.Cover and let the dough prove.Heat the oil and fry the mince with the chopped onion and dill.Cool the filling.Cut the dough into rounds, fill, and seal.Bake at 200°C until golden.Old-country vareniki with fried onionThe Mousekewitz family's taste of the old countryHow to make itAs written, serves 4Potato and cheese dumplings boiled then fried in butter with golden onion, served with sour cream and dill.Mash 500g boiled potatoes with 100g grated cheddar and salt.Cut 24 rounds from 2 sheets fresh pasta or use gow gee wrappers, fill each with a spoon of potato, fold and press shut.Boil in batches for 3 minutes until they float.Fry 1 sliced onion in 40g butter until golden, add the dumplings and toss 2 minutes.Serve with 150g sour cream and dill.MainsMama's beetroot and cabbage borschtBeef stock soup with beetroot, carrot, cabbage and potato, sharpened with vinegarHow to make it3 beetroots2 carrots1/4 cabbage2 potatoes1.5 L beef stock2 tbsp vinegar1 bunch dill120g sour cream8 slices of rye breadGrate the beetroot and carrots, shred the cabbage and dice the potatoes.Simmer all the vegetables in the stock until tender.Add the vinegar and plenty of dill.Serve with a big spoon of sour cream and rye bread.Mama's cheese blintzes with berry sauceMama Mousekewitz's cooking, carried from Shostka to New YorkHow to make itAs written, serves 4Thin crêpes rolled around sweet lemon ricotta, fried golden in butter and served with warm berry sauce and sour cream.Whisk 150g plain flour, 3 eggs, 350ml milk and a pinch of salt.Cook 8 thin crêpes in a buttered pan, one side only.Mix 400g ricotta, 100g cream cheese, 50g sugar and lemon zest.Fill the cooked side, fold into parcels and fry in 30g butter for 2 minutes a side.Simmer 300g frozen berries with 2 tbsp sugar for 5 minutes and serve with sour cream.SweetsShostka honey cakeSpiced honey cake with brown sugar and coffee, baked in a tinHow to make it250g honey125ml vegetable oil3 eggs150g brown sugar125ml strong coffee300g plain flour2 tsp baking powder2 tsp mixed spiceHeat the oven to 170°C and line a tin.Whisk the honey, oil, eggs, sugar and coffee.Fold in the flour, baking powder and mixed spice and pour into the tin.Bake until a skewer comes out clean.Cool in the tin.DrinksPapa's fiddle-night Russian teaHot black tea in glasses with lemon, raspberry jam stirred in for sweetnessHow to make it4 tsp black tea leaves1 L boiling water1 lemon100g raspberry jamBrew the tea in just-boiled water and strain into heatproof glasses.Add a lemon slice to each and serve with jam for stirring in.
